post.summary: Logs in with information
post.description:
Change History:
  • Introduced in v8.5

Notes:

If you enable password encryption in "Web.config," you must comply with the following rules:
  • Use the encryption keys in "Web.config" (you can override them).
  • Encode in ANSI.
  • Use HMACSHA256 methods to encode passwords.
  • Remove all '-' characters.
  • Lower the strings.
// Example of a C# methodpublic string Encryption(string key, string text)
{
var bytesKey = Encoding.Default.GetBytes(key);
var bytesText = Encoding.Default.GetBytes(text);
var hash256 = new HMACSHA256(bytesKey);
var result = hash256.ComputeHash(bytesText);
return BitConverter.ToString(result).Replace("-", "").ToLower();
}
// Example of a PHP methodfunction($key, $text)
{
$hash = hash_hmac('sha256', $text, $key);
$hash = str_replace('-', '', $hash);
return strtolower($hash);
}
Returns a token. You must set the token in the authorization property of the request header with the "Bearer" type.
Authorization: Bearer eaa61c7241bd4cc9449fa25bb4e57ff1

Fetches a list of entities by parameters
get.description:
Change History:
  • Introduced in v10.1
  • Fixed execution of queries using "or" statement in v11.1
Filter

Filters are composed of expressions. Each expression is separated by:

And
& encoded as %26 in parameter value
Or
| encoded as %21 in parameter value

Each expression is composed of three parts.
First, an available field name for the current entity.
Second, the operator:

Equal
= encoded as %3D in parameter value
Less than
< encoded as %3C in parameter value
Less than or equal to
<= encoded as %3C%3D in parameter value
Greater than
> encoded as %3E in parameter value
Greater than or equal to
>= encoded as %3E%3D in parameter value
Starts with
[ encoded as %5B in parameter value
Ends with
] encoded as %5D in parameter value
Contains
: encoded as %3A in parameter value
Range
{ encoded as %7B in parameter value

You can use "!" before the operator for negative conditions (%21 once encoded in parameter value). 

Example: "!=" // It means "Not equal"

The last part is the value to fetch. For a String or DateTime, you must use double quotes (").

When using the Range operator, values are seperated by ",".

Example : GET localhost/api/data/fetch/ItemEntity?filter=Item="001-0001"|Stock=true// Search item "001-0001" or all of items which are stockExample : GET localhost/api/data/fetch/ItemEntity?filter=Item!{"001-0001,001-0000"&Stock=true// Search items not "001-0001","001-0000" and all items which are stockExample : GET localhost/api/data/fetch/ItemEntity?filter=Id{10000003,10000004// Search ids 10000003,10000004

Sort

Each sort is separated by ",".
You must use an available field name for the current entity.
You can use the descending symbol "-" before the field name, otherwise it will be sorted by ascending.

Example : GET /api/data/ItemEntity/search?sort=-CreationDate,Code// Sort descending by creation date, then by ascending code

Fields

Response will only contain entered fields for each entity. Each field is separated by a semi-colon ";" or a comma "," or an ampersand "&" character.
You must use an available field name for the current entity.

// Example with a semi-colonId;Item
// Example with a commaId,Item
// Example with an ampersandId&Item

Result

The result will be a list of selected entities. To know the schema for each entity, see the request for the new entity.
If Fields have been entered the entity schema will contain only these fields. 

Example : GET /api/data/properties/ItemEntity/new

parameters.name: related
parameters.description: If set to true, loads related entities (false by default)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit (limited by the company parameter by default)

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: The fields separated by a semi-colon ";" or a comma "," or an ampersand "&" character.
